summary: Loads Alembic .abc geometry, transforms, object paths, attributes, and multi-frame animation into POP GPU memory. Polymesh, curves, and points are converted to POP triangles, quads, line strips, point primitives, and attributes.

key_params.name: objectpath
key_params.note: Object path or all objects from the Alembic archive

key_params.name: sampleratemode
key_params.note: Use file FPS or custom sample rate for animation playback

key_params.name: initialize
key_params.note: Reset animation to its initial state

key_params.name: indexunit
key_params.note: Index unit: index, frames, seconds, or fraction

key_params.note: Enable trim start and end controls

key_params.note: Hold, cycle, or mirror before trim start

key_params.name: textendright
key_params.note: Hold, cycle, or mirror after trim end

key_concepts: Alembic In POP imports Alembic geometry archives into POP GPU memory, including polymesh, curves, points, transforms, object paths, and multi-frame sequences.
Object Path can load one selected Alembic object or all objects; duplicate attribute names across selected objects may be promoted to vertex attributes when classes differ.
Transform mode separates no transform, static local, static world, and dynamic transform handling; interpolation only applies when the source geometry has dynamic samples and transform data.
The Play page supports timeline-locked playback, specified index playback, sequential playback, cueing, trim ranges, and left/right extension behavior for animated archives.
Alembic attribute scopes and types do not map one-to-one to POPs: supported scopes become point, vertex, or primitive attributes, while unsupported or oversized types are converted or omitted.
common_gotchas: Some Alembic attribute types are converted or unsupported; strings, bools, chars, and 8/16-bit float colors do not map one-to-one.
Faces with more than four vertices become closed line strips rather than polygon meshes.
Duplicate attribute names across selected objects may be converted to vertex attributes when classes differ.
